text: The ovens were humming, very low, filling the air with yeast and burnt sugar, like a sort of lullaby. Elias wiped some flour off his forearms. Checked the clock. 3:17 AM Thursday. There was a worn paperback on the front counter on the glass display case. The Shadow of the Wind. He picked it up. Dog-eared pages. It had been there 6 weeks. Normally he'd just pop it in the return bin, assume it's a confused customer who thought the bakery late night drop slot was a library return, but tonight it was a bit warmer than the cool shop air. He opened it to the bookmarked page. A folded square of lined paper slipped out, fluttered to the counter. He hesitated, then opened it. Jagged handwriting, hurried. It said, "I know you're reading it. Keep going. Page 204 changes everything." His heart hammered hard. Sharp rhythm against the quiet hum of the mixers. He looked around the empty shop, shadows long across the tiled floor. No one was there. Looked back at the note. Then back at the book. With trembling fingers turned to page 204. The text blurred before his eyes. He closed it, pressed it flat against the counter, and reached for his pen.
